root_cause_analysis.mechanism: src/index.css's `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block (comment: 'keep opacity transitions only') set `transition-duration: 100ms !important` on every element but never restricted `transition-property`, so any element with no explicit `transition-property` declaration kept the CSS initial value `all`. Input (src/components/ui/input.tsx) declares no transition utility at all, so it falls into this case; Button (src/components/ui/button.tsx) explicitly declares Tailwind's `transition-colors` utility (an explicit property list: color, background-color, border-color, outline-color, text-decoration-color, fill, stroke, and gradient-stop custom properties -- notably not box-shadow), so it was never affected by the `all` fallback and its ring stayed instant. Tailwind 4 also compiles `focus-visible:outline-none` to an actual `outline: none`, so the focus box-shadow ring is the only cue for the two inputs. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the block's blanket duration override newly activated a real 100ms CSS transition on `box-shadow` for the inputs, which previously had no transition on that property at all (initial duration 0s outside reduced motion), so their focus ring animates in from its unfocused (fully transparent) value instead of applying instantly. The release-gate probe samples computed style synchronously in the same tick as the Tab keypress with no wait, so it can observe the transparent starting frame of that now-animated transition; this is inherently timing-dependent, which is why not every repeated sample in the diagnosis run hit the transparent frame.
root_cause_analysis.why_default_context_passed: Outside prefers-reduced-motion, no rule sets transition-duration on box-shadow for the inputs, so it stays at the browser's initial 0s value and the ring change is applied on the same frame -- no race for the probe to observe.

fix.change: Added `transition-property: opacity !important;` to the existing `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block, restricting what any element under reduced motion is allowed to transition to opacity only -- matching the block's pre-existing comment intent ('keep opacity transitions only') exactly. Non-opacity property changes (box-shadow, outline-color, border-color, etc.) now apply instantly under reduced motion instead of animating over the forced 100ms duration.

e2e_regression_coverage.note: New Playwright spec against a production build served by the existing e2e webServer (scripts/build-e2e-server.mjs + vite preview), using page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark', reducedMotion: 'reduce' }) in a beforeEach. `reducedMotion` is only documented as a `TestOptions.contextOptions` field (node_modules/playwright/types/test.d.ts ~line 7501), not a top-level `test.use()` key -- unlike `colorScheme`, which is a first-class top-level TestOptions field (same file, line 7084) -- so an initial `test.use({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })` was silently ignored while `colorScheme: 'dark'` took effect. Verified directly: with that top-level `test.use`, `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` was `false` while `(prefers-color-scheme: dark)` was `true`; switching to `page.emulateMedia` set both correctly. This is a testOptions API-shape correction, not a browser/environment defect.
